comments.author: @JJørgensen
comments.text:
As someone who was living in Czech Republic for 20 years and still coming back there, I can agree with everything you said in this video except the "adult thing" in first chapter. This was famous during the 90s but it is far gone now. Also I can contribute with many details. Just some:
Czech Republic is known also as one of the safest country in the entire world to live. Criminality is very very low there and the main thing, there are no "no-go zones". In Czech Republic, there are almost no homeless people, no big drug problems and so. You can NOT own a gun just because you want. There are very strict rules with hard exams to obtain a permission for it. 
The country is known also for one special thing: 73% of population live in their own houses/apartments, I mean they are the owners. 
Taxes are low and even property tax is still very low. Example: if you own a 200 square meters 5 bedroom house with 2000 square meters lot, you pay only around 200 to 500 USD (depends on exact place) per year as property tax. This is one of many reason why many foreigners are moving to Czech Republic to live.
On the other side, for example, the cost of gas (petrol/diesel) is double the price in USA (7.6 USD per US gallon in the moment I am writing this comment)
Prague is one of the most beautiful cities, the historic downtown surrounded with new modern districts and large suburbs all around. I always love to travel the city using the dense tram network, with great views.
